learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling students to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan in the context of the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Understands the relationship between the analysis of the company and its environment to establish its behavior (types of strategies) and results.

Identifies and knows how to adopt the main strategic and tactical decisions in operations management, starting with the selection of potential locations for the company's facilities and the most appropriate productive processes.
Knows work organization through different methods studies, time measurement, and work incentive systems.
Recognizes the importance of occupational risk prevention in company activities and knows how to identify the necessary elements to organize said prevention.
Knows and can use different production planning, scheduling, and control models to meet customer needs.

Identifies the key parameters of the logistics chain (Supply Chain Management), which encompasses all company activities related to the procurement, storage, and distribution of materials and products to ensure a certain service level at the lowest possible cost.

Learns the concept and philosophy of Total Quality, as well as the necessary methods and actions for global quality measurement, planning, and control, to achieve the competitive advantage the company needs.

syllabus_topics: Block I. Decisions on location, productive processes, and work organization
Block II. Decisions on Planning, Scheduling, and Control of operations
Block IV. Decisions on Industrial Quality

assessment_methods.method: Group practices applying concepts and using software tools
Individual practical exercises using software tools
Individual written test (theoretical and practical questions)

assessment_rules: Students can choose between two evaluation paths. For continuous evaluation, group practices account for 15%, individual practical exercises for 10%, and an individual written test for 75%. A minimum score of 4.5 out of 10 in the written test is required for it to be averaged with other continuous assessment activities. For global evaluation, there are two exams: the first accounts for 75% of the final grade, and the second for 25%. A minimum score of 4.5 out of 10 in the first written exam is required for it to be averaged with the second exam.
